findings.source_passage: I knew not how this consciousness at last glided away from me; but waking in the morning, I shudderingly remembered it all, and for days and weeks and months afterwards I lost myself in confounding attempts to explain the mystery. Nay, to this very hour, I often puzzle myself with it.
findings.source_locator: end of the childhood nightmare paragraph, after 'the horrid spell would be broken'
findings.why_it_matters: This closing coda to the supernatural-hand episode carries significant interpretive weight — it establishes Ishmael's characteristic pattern of dwelling on inexplicable experience and frames the mystery as ongoing. Its omission severs the philosophical resonance that links the childhood vision to the novel's broader metaphysical concerns.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the passage verbatim or near-verbatim before the transition paragraph beginning 'Now, take away the awful fear.' It is brief and cuts nothing else.

findings.source_passage: for the time my curiosity getting the better of my breeding. Nevertheless, a man like Queequeg you don't see every day, he and his ways were well worth unusual regarding.
findings.source_locator: end of the paragraph beginning 'Meanwhile, I lay quietly eyeing him'
findings.why_it_matters: This self-deprecating, colloquially rhythmed aside is voice-establishing — Ishmael's mock-genteel self-correction ('curiosity getting the better of my breeding') followed by the blunt Americanism 'you don't see every day' is exactly the register that defines his narrative persona. Dropping it flattens the ironic self-awareness.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the two sentences to the end of that paragraph: 'for the time my curiosity getting the better of my breeding. Nevertheless, a man like Queequeg you don't see every day, he and his ways were well worth unusual regarding.'

findings.source_passage: If he had not been a small degree civilized, he very probably would not have troubled himself with boots at all; but then, if he had not been still a savage, he never would have dreamt of getting under the bed to put them on.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the logical pay-off to the 'caterpillar nor butterfly / undergraduate' argument — the syllogism about boots and savagery is the comic and analytical climax of the passage. Without it, the transition-stage conceit hangs without its punchline.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-part conditional sentence immediately after 'His education was not yet completed. He was an undergraduate.' before the description of him emerging from under the bed.

findings.source_passage: Afterwards I wondered the less at this operation when I came to know of what fine steel the head of a harpoon is made, and how exceedingly sharp the long straight edges are always kept.
findings.why_it_matters: This brief remark is a characteristic Ishmaelian aside linking comic domestic observation to the professional world of whaling — a small but typical example of how the narrator foreshadows the trade's technical reality within everyday anecdote. Its loss is minor but consistent with a pattern of trimming Ishmael's retrospective asides.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the sentence after 'Rogers's best cutlery with a vengeance.' It is one sentence and costs very little word budget.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; two medium-severity omissions (the childhood-mystery coda and the self-deprecating breeding/curiosity aside) flatten Ishmael's voice and sever interpretive threads, but do not individually trigger regeneration, and with only two medium findings the threshold of three is not reached — draft passes with recommended restoration of the missing passages.
